[02] page 02 of 8learn / 学ぶ

how to learn Japanese_

the question I get asked the most. I'm answering it once, properly, here.

02.1

my answer

答え
the short answer:結論

learning Japanese is easier than you think. you need four things: vocabulary, grammar, speaking and listening. the rest is keeping it fun.

  1. 1
    learn to read first

    memorize hiragana and katakana, your own way. flashcards work well. don't wait until they're perfect: they get stronger as you learn.

  2. 2
    learn sentences, not single words

    a word sticks when you meet it in a sentence, and every sentence teaches you grammar too.

  3. 3
    talk to people

    use HelloTalk to make friends who are learning too. join the voice rooms, speak, and don't be shy. you're supposed to make mistakes. it's also how I trained my ears.

  4. 4
    keep the motivation

    if you can't read anything at the start, you'll give up. so romaji is fine for now, and it should be fun, not a chore.

  5. 5
    lock in

    30 minutes to 1 hour a day. that's about 3 months to N5.

my path
started in 2022, passed N3 in 2024.12 and N2 in 2025.12
start here
N5, from zero >

    03.2

    kana

    かな
    how I learned them:わたしの方法

    I just memorized them first. then every new sentence I learned made them stronger. so memorize them your own way, and don't wait until they're perfect to move on. flashcards work well.

    tap any letter to hear it. this device has no Japanese voice, so sound is off here.

    the sounds that trip beginners up 注意

    long vowels
    おばさん obasan aunt · おばあさん obaasan grandmother. in katakana, ー makes it long: コーヒー koohii coffee
    small っ
    a tiny pause that doubles the next sound: きって kitte stamp · きて kite come
    small ゃゅょ
    join the letter before into one sound: きゃ kya, not きや kiya
    は へ を
    as particles they're read wa, e and o: わたしは watashi wa · がっこうへ gakkou e · みずを mizu o

    romaji here follows the kana letter by letter, so おう is ou and ああ is aa.

    move on when: you can read them, even slowly. they get stronger in vocabulary >

    語彙

    the JLPT hasn't published an official word list since 2010, so the words here follow the N5 lists most learners use.

    each day
    review the old words first, then learn new ones

    03.5

    listening and speaking

    聴解と会話

    listening 聴解

    listening is a third of the N5 score, with its own pass mark, so don't skip it. it's something you train on your own: every word and sentence on this page has ▶, so listen before you read.

    practise with
    the official JLPT sample questions > free, with N5 listening audio, its script and the answers
    how I trained my ears:わたしの方法

    on HelloTalk. I just kept talking to people, Japanese people and people learning Japanese, and they replied in Japanese. most of my conversations were in Japanese, and that's what improved my listening.

    speaking on HelloTalk 会話

    the JLPT doesn't test speaking, but speaking is how you actually start using Japanese. most of mine came from HelloTalk >, the same place my listening came from.

    use it to
    make friends who are learning too, and learn together
    not as
    a study app. the key is to have fun
    voice rooms
    use them a lot. speak, and don't be shy
    mistakes
    you're supposed to make them
    in time
    you'll learn to hold a basic conversation
    when
    once you have some sentences to say
    03.6

    ready check

    腕試し

    you're ready to book the test when you've done every unit's vocabulary and grammar, and you can pass the official sample in real test time.

    1. the official sample, timed 模擬試験

    open the official N5 sample > and use this timer. it runs the three parts in the same times as the real test.

    vocabulary20:00

    listening time can be a little different on the day, depending on the length of the recordings.

    2. check your score 合格点

    vocabulary, grammar, reading
    at least 38 of 120
    listening
    at least 19 of 60
    total
    at least 80 of 180

    you need all three. a high total with a low listening score is still a fail.

    3. book the test 申し込み

    when
    twice a year, in July and December. some cities outside Japan only hold one of them
    where
    through the test's local host in your city. find yours on the JLPT site >
    tip
    registration closes well before test day, so check your city's dates early
    want help before the test?レッスン

    I can go through the sample with you and fix what's tripping you up. message me >

    04.4

    reading

    読解

    the passages here are written the way the N4 reading questions are: short notes, longer essays and information search, where you find one fact in a timetable or price list.

    me
    I used Shin Kanzen Master (新完全マスター) a lot. my grammar and vocab book was written all in Japanese too, so just reading it was reading practice
    every day
    HelloTalk. my friends always reply in Japanese, so I read Japanese every day. it's great for daily conversation, but it won't give you textbook vocabulary, so do both

    how to answer 解き方

    1. read the question before the passage, so you know what you're looking for.
    2. find the line in the passage it points to. in information search, read the ※ notes too. that's where the traps are.
    3. check every option against that line, not against what sounds right. if it isn't written there, it isn't the answer.

    after you answer, every option tells you why it's right or wrong, and the line that holds the answer turns lime.

    N2_

    the level many jobs and universities in Japan ask for. the news, work, and the Japanese people actually use every day.

    06.1

    start here

    はじめに
    pace
    your own. move on when you're ready, not by the calendar
    me
    I only studied about a week for N2, because I was rushing, and I passed in 2025.12. I used Shin Kanzen Master again
    how long
    I wouldn't recommend it, but you can pass N2 in one week. I did
    focus
    vocabulary. there were a lot of words in the exam I couldn't read. if I'd built my vocabulary first, it would have been easy

    that's why this level is built around words: 20 units, each with more words than at N3.

    at least 19 of 60
    total
    at least 100 of 180

    you need all four. at 100, N1 has the highest total pass mark of all five levels.

    3. book the test 申し込み

    the same as N5: July and December, through your city's local host. N5 details >

    my story_

    why a Singaporean designer is trying to study in Japan, and where I am on the way.

    08.1

    how it started

    はじまり

    I have a friend, a Singaporean designer, who studied at a school in Japan. I've always loved his work. watching him made me realize that design in Japan could be so much more. it isn't just about being pretty. there's a reason behind everything. and when I speak Japanese, I feel more confident. I want to know so much more about Japan, and one day I want to express my own designs in Japanese
